seo.title: Cone Volume Calculator - Hopper Silo
seo.description: Cone Volume Calculator — Calculate volume of a cone or hopper from diameter and height, for silos, hoppers, and conical tank bottoms with instant results & multiple unit support.

content.introduction: Calculate the volume of a right circular cone — used for silo bottoms, hopper design, conical tank sections, and material flow calculations. A cone holds exactly 1/3 of the equivalent cylinder.

faq.a: Frustum volume = (πh/3)(R² + Rr + r²) where R and r are the two radii. This calculator handles full cones only.

faq.q: How much angle for mass flow in a hopper?
faq.a: For most bulk solids, a hopper half-angle of 15-20° from vertical ensures mass flow. Steeper for sticky materials.

faq.q: How do I convert cone volume between m³ and ft³?
faq.a: 1 m³ = 35.315 ft³. For example, a 2 m³ hopper = 70.6 ft³. Conversely, divide ft³ by 35.315 to get m³.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion for Cone Volume
sections.body:
**Volume units**

- 1 m³ = 1000 L = 35.315 ft³
- 1 ft³ = 0.02832 m³ = 28.317 L
- 1 US gal = 3.785 L

**Length units**

- 1 m = 3.28084 ft
- 1 inch = 25.4 mm

Cone volume V = (1/3)πr²h requires consistent length units. For a frustum (truncated cone), V = (πh/3)(R² + Rr + r²). Convert radius and height to the same unit before computing.
